shoal_e10_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred One, Yue reached the ordinary inspection lane before active loading began. Two neighboring sheds stood beyond its boundary: Shed Three, held by the packing partnership, and privately owned Shed Six farther along the quay. Their shared public approach did not make their goods, lamps, or staff the same. A new thirty-six-copper safety-session account funded the qualified outside inspection and follow-up. Yue had come as an invited observer, carrying her own notes and no lender's instrument.

shoal_e10_morning_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_01.text: Yan showed the visitors where the observer rope would move when the scheduled crane began. A line that stayed fixed all day would become wrong by noon. Yue checked the ordinary public exit and the location of the staffed alarm post. Neither depended on her being able to circulate. The school marker test was behind her, and its setup was absent. Today she needed eyes, a clear path, and a reliable distinction between what she saw and what someone told her afterward.

shoal_e10_morning_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_02.text: The safety-session supervisor had eighteen copper for the two accepted visits, the clerk four for the specified record work, materials ten for actual permitted corrections, and notices four for their defined dispatch. No part employed Yue or bought every shed's maintenance forever. The owners retained their own ordinary duties and accounts. The supervisor would inspect the offered exterior lane and unloaded safety arrangements, recording what remained outside that scope.

shoal_e10_morning_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_03.text: He Ming arrived for the packing partnership with the names of its current authorized representatives. He did not speak for privately owned Shed Six. The owner of that shed sent a current steward to the offered lane inspection, with no public access to all private stock. The distinction irritated two visitors who wanted one meeting to reveal the whole harbor. Yue understood their impatience and asked the actual relevant question: who controlled the lamp and waste arrangements beside each current work route?

shoal_e10_morning_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_04.text: The partnership showed its ordinary lamp location inside Shed Three and the separate exterior maintenance table. The private steward described Shed Six's lamp brackets and current responsible hands, offering the listed routine check but not a secret supplier appendix. The supervisor checked the visible route clearances. A permitted list did not prove every future movement harmless. It established who should act when the arrangement changed, which was more practical than calling either building generally safe.

shoal_e10_morning_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_05.text: At the exterior maintenance table near Shed Three, an ordinary worker prepared a small permitted heat tool under the qualified supervisor's setup. Fuel, sand, clear distance, and an assigned stop were checked. Yue stood outside the boundary and supplied no energy. The task would mend a plain metal fastening, not qualify a freight-signal device. The worker had done such work before. Familiarity made the check shorter, not unnecessary.

shoal_e10_morning_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_06.text: A gust lifted a light waste rag from behind the table's leg. Its corner crossed the tool's hot edge and flared. The worker stopped on the supervisor's call, isolated the tool, and stepped into the clear route. The assigned ordinary assistant used the prepared sand to contain the small flame. Yan kept observers behind their rope. Yue felt her hand twitch toward a release stroke that had no qualified application here and kept it at her own side.

shoal_e10_morning_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_07.text: The rag burned through before the assistant finished covering it. It had held a small quantity of oily waste from an earlier ordinary cleaning task, not a secret talisman fuel. The event stayed local to the exterior table. No person was burned, no shed caught, and no qi barrier appeared across the quay. The supervisor closed that heat task immediately and preserved the actual burned waste for its owner-controlled fault record.

shoal_e10_morning_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_08.text: Two ordinary workers had seen the rag lift before the flame. Yue had seen the corner cross the hot edge and the assigned sand response. The supervisor wrote their separate angles and did not merge them into one flawless witness. The private steward had been looking at the lane post and had not seen ignition. He could still confirm the subsequent closed task. Independent accounts gave the small event more shape precisely because each stopped where sight had stopped.

shoal_e10_morning_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_09.text: The waste tray's cover had not been secured after its earlier use. The responsible owner accepted the actual correction: waste moved into a closed appropriate container, the fastening task stayed suspended, and the outside lane was checked for further loose material. The ten-copper materials line covered the accepted closure and ordinary correction within its scope. The assigned workers did it before lunch, not after a future disaster taught everyone to care.

shoal_e10_morning_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_10.text: Yan required the public observer rope farther from the heat table when any later permitted setup resumed. The owner replaced the damaged tray arrangement and requested the qualified follow-up on Day Three Hundred Three. Yue would not be required to attend it. A small warning had changed actual work and a real boundary. It had not granted the exterior inspector unlimited access to the neighboring private shed or proved that every other lamp shared this particular fault.

shoal_e10_morning_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_11.text: Rong heard of the flare and asked whether the school marker had caused it. The current records showed the ordinary heat tool and loose waste, with Yue outside the work setup and no cultivation input. He withdrew the question's implied cause after reading the dates. A rumor could join two nearby stories because the same woman appeared in both. The independently observed ignition and stopped ordinary response gave the port a way to separate them.

shoal_e10_morning_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_12.text: By the time loading began, the exterior heat task remained closed and the corrected waste arrangement was in place. Visitors left the active lane as agreed. The crane crew took the route under its current ordinary command. Yue watched from the public boundary rather than returning to inspect because she now felt invested in the warning. A qualified correction had its own follow-up and responsible people. Her alarm did not become a private license to patrol every workplace.

shoal_e10_morning_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_morning_13.text: The afternoon source appointment followed the access created by the earlier wage receiving. A public named group could read offered posted movement states and ask current open questions. A confidential individual process could compare particular permitted times inside a restricted file. Neither would expose every store's contents. Yue took only the invitation she actually held, leaving the contained exterior flare's independent record at its proper desk.

shoal_e10_receiving_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_receiving_gate.text: The inspection's public lane had closed to visitors when active loading began. Yue's later appointment concerned records offered through the actually completed wage receiving. Those permissions came from a named public request or consenting individual files, with different detail and limits. The flare had not enlarged them. She went to the desk authorized by her actual invitation.

shoal_e10_open_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_01.text: He Ming's group met the public clerk beneath the posted receiving board. Its completed joint statement had obtained a published reply and current access to offered public route explanations. The group could ask why a request mark was later described as a delivery. It could not demand a private supplier file merely because names stood on a public receipt. Yue attended as the separately invited narrow witness, not as the owner of the group's questions.

shoal_e10_open_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_02.text: The posted movement record named one carrier request entered before the medicine boat arrived. A supplier's public summary had shortened that into goods sent. The clerk showed that no carried mark belonged to the request at that time. A later dispatch had its own date. The difference mattered to the shared wage gap without proving intentional deceit. He Ming asked for the summary's wording to be corrected so another reader would not inherit the same false sequence.

shoal_e10_open_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_03.text: The supplier representative accepted a public wording correction after checking the relevant offered record. She did not release the private customer prices attached to her full file. The group retained a copy of the corrected public summary and the actual previous wording. Erasing the old sentence would have hidden why the question arose. Yue witnessed the correction and stopped her note at the offered public facts. A narrower error had been established, not a whole criminal account.

shoal_e10_open_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_04.text: The signatory who had lost a prospective commission said a correct sentence did not replace her work. He Ming agreed and kept her permitted visibility-risk note separate. The supplier representative could answer this summary error without buying the merchant's independent withdrawn offer. Nobody asked Yue to call a corrected record compensation. A public process had changed what the port would publish while leaving a person's material disappointment intact.

shoal_e10_open_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_05.text: Another worker wanted the summary to name whoever wrote the bad sentence. The current public process could request that responsible attribution if the source owner offered it under the proper scope. It could not infer a guilty name from the handwriting shape. The representative said she would answer the actual attribution question later. Yue kept it pending. The group could insist on accountability without making an unverified accusation its fastest path.

shoal_e10_open_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_06.text: From the public board, they could also read the exterior safety-session closure: the contained flare's heat task was stopped, its loose oily waste removed into a closed appropriate container, and a qualified follow-up scheduled. The source named Shed Three's exterior maintenance table. It did not describe Shed Six as inspected inside. He Ming asked the clerk to read the locations aloud because two listeners had been treating adjacent numbers as one building.

shoal_e10_open_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_07.text: The correction would matter if a later claim said the whole lane had been declared safe by today's visit. The public page supported only its offered exterior scope and actual corrections. Yue did not add a prediction of another fire. She knew the small flare had been contained and its responsible owner had acted. She did not know what every worker would move in the private shed tomorrow, and the honest page left that fact unclaimed.

shoal_e10_open_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_08.text: The group sent its current public questions through the named clerk before leaving. The four-copper notice line in the safety account did not pay these separate wage messages; their own group source covered the ordinary permitted request process. Yue accepted no new paid term. She could attend an offered later public reply without acquiring the whole harbor's watch duty. He Ming checked that the posted sheet remained readable to people who had missed the meeting.

shoal_e10_open_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_09.text: At the lane junction, one named signatory decided she would stop speaking publicly for a while. Her earlier consent remained valid for the received statement, but future naming required a new choice. The group accepted her limit and found another willing speaker for its next question. Public solidarity could continue without consuming the same visible person every time. Yue watched the handover and remembered that a brave hour was still an hour someone could end.

shoal_e10_open_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_open_10.text: She left with permitted public corrections and no private carrier attachments. The completed joint statement had opened a visible record path and exposed workers to actual commercial risk. Its public access could later support a supplier-account challenge, but it would not answer every hidden technical condition. Yue had seen the exterior flare independently and the summary wording corrected. Those facts would remain separate when a more frightening event asked people to join every warning into one inevitable story.

shoal_e10_restricted_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_01.text: The restricted receiver admitted Yue only after the relevant worker confirmed the offered comparison scope. His confidential wage appointment had obtained a particular file path, not open access to every carrier's papers. The comparison concerned the request, actual dispatch, and receiving dates relevant to his route claim. Private medical records and customer prices stayed excluded. Yue put her outside inspection note away before approaching the file table. A new question deserved its own permission.

shoal_e10_restricted_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_02.text: The worker's retained request had been entered before the medicine boat arrived. A later carrier attachment showed the actual dispatch date, different from the public shorthand he had heard. The receiver compared the two without letting Yue read unoffered commercial lines. A dated movement could clarify the individual's gap while remaining unavailable for general publication. The worker authorized a narrow received conclusion for his claim, not a public portrait of everyone whose goods shared the boat.

shoal_e10_restricted_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_03.text: The carrier representative acknowledged that a shortened description had joined request and dispatch. She corrected the permitted individual comparison note and kept the original wording in the restricted record. The current file did not establish intentional fraud or a private technical defect. The worker could ask further under the proper process. Yue witnessed which corrected note he actually received and declined to retain the underlying attachment in her personal notebook.

shoal_e10_restricted_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_04.text: The two other confidential cases had their own states. One had supplied its missing confirmation and awaited the relevant reply; the other still needed an employer clause explanation. The first worker's clearer movement dates did not settle either automatically. Shared travel had produced different agreements. Yue could care about all three without pretending her permitted view of one file made her an advocate holding every other person's private claim.

shoal_e10_restricted_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_05.text: He Ming asked for a general statement the group might use publicly. The worker authorized a single sentence: a requested movement and actual dispatch had different dates in his checked record. He withheld the name, agreement, and full attachment. He Ming could pose a general question from that offered sentence; he could not publish the private evidence as if the group owned it. The restricted path had created detail while limiting collective visibility.

shoal_e10_restricted_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_06.text: At the receiver's public counter, Yue read the exterior safety-session closure separately from the confidential file. The small flare's heat task was stopped, loose oily waste secured, and qualified follow-up scheduled at Shed Three's exterior maintenance table. No inside inspection of neighboring Shed Six had been declared. The private date record supplied no broader safety scope. Two accurate accounts could sit on the same desk without becoming proof of a connection neither had observed.

shoal_e10_restricted_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_07.text: The worker asked whether the flare explained his carrier delay. Its date came after the actual medicine receiving, and its location belonged to a different current task. Yue showed the public dates and refused the proposed link. He laughed at himself, then said every new trouble seemed to want the same explanation. The restricted record could make one uncertainty smaller. It could not give him a cause big enough to hold everything that had hurt his week.

shoal_e10_restricted_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_08.text: The receiver retained the protected attachment under its existing procedure. Yue kept only the worker's permitted narrow conclusion and her own witnessed receiving note. A later supplier-account question might use this path if the owner consented again. It would not become a public source by waiting long enough. The current claim had an applicable detail, while the group's immediate published-reply process remained unperformed through her earlier chosen hour.

shoal_e10_restricted_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_09.text: Outside, the worker decided to keep his next ordinary work appointment rather than attend another public meeting that afternoon. He had accepted a separate paid stock task under its own terms. His private claim would continue through the receiver without requiring his body in every room. Yue respected the departure. A confidential process could protect time as well as paper, though it gave other workers less public evidence with which to press their shared demand.

shoal_e10_restricted_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_restricted_10.text: She left without a private file in her pack or a mandate to inspect a supplier's apparatus. The individual record had clarified dates and retained its restricted scope. The independently observed exterior flare remained a different event, with its own corrected owner arrangement. Later danger might tempt a crowd to treat every earlier warning as one story. Yue would have to preserve the narrow facts even when a larger explanation sounded more satisfying.

shoal_e10_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_01.text: On Day Three Hundred Two, the partnership's exterior heat table stayed closed. Ordinary fastening work moved to a separately approved workshop whose setup already covered it. The owner paid that worker under its own current account rather than charging Yue's finished restoration term. A delay remained on the partnership's repair list. The small flare had cost time and a damaged tray. Its limited containment had not made the whole event free.

shoal_e10_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_02.text: The supervisor returned on Day Three Hundred Three for the accepted follow-up. The closed waste container was present, its responsible worker identified, and the new observer distance marked. The corrected heat setup passed the qualified local check within its offered scope. He signed only that setup and lane condition. Privately owned Shed Six retained its own inside maintenance duty. A neighboring visitor could read the actual distinction on the posted report.

shoal_e10_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_03.text: Yan's crew rehearsed the current staffed alarm route during a quiet ordinary work interval. One runner found a cart narrowing the approach and asked its owner to move it before rehearsal continued. The owner had thought a momentary stop would be harmless. Yan explained that an emergency route must be available before it was needed. No emergency occurred in the drill. The inconvenience taught a practical fact without inventing a catastrophe to prove the foreman's judgment.

shoal_e10_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_04.text: Yue attended the public beginning and left when the crew moved into its actual paid task. She did not perform the runner's route with qi or acquire a rescue qualification from watching. The mark she carried away was ordinary: the alarm post could be reached from the public side if that cart space stayed clear. Knowing a route could make later action possible. It would not guarantee the route stayed clear under a different day's movement.

shoal_e10_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_05.text: On Day Three Hundred Four, the clinic messenger passed the yard carrying no medicine, only a current receiving question from his employer. He had eaten before leaving this time. Yue greeted him and did not join the errand unasked. Their acquaintance had survived a useful week without making every later task shared. He said the potter had asked whether her cup still stood upright. She said it did if she remembered which way to turn it.

shoal_e10_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_06.text: At the public beach, the shore keeper's notice asked boat owners to report lost net locations through the actual ordinary channel. The dead seal had not become proof of a named fisherman's guilt. A fisherman reported a line lost farther along the shoal, with its approximate position and date. The keeper accepted the report without promising retrieval in dangerous water. A later permitted cleanup might reduce a hazard. It would not return the animal already dead.

shoal_e10_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_07.text: He Ming's packing group received clarification of its offered corner hours and chose its actual participants for the month. Some former workers stayed with their newer routes. The fruit seller accepted a limited slot that fit his current stock. Yue bought an orange and listened to his complaint that the permit fee had a more reliable appetite than any customer. He did not want her to fix the fee that morning. He wanted her to enjoy the joke before paying.

shoal_e10_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_08.text: Song Mei's venue search brought a current offer from a warehouse keeper. She inspected the proposed public room and refused because the exit route crossed active loading while the audience would still be inside. The offered price was good. She declined it anyway and lost that date's income opportunity. Yue could see how her earlier insistence on a bounded inspected room had costs that never became an uplifting public notice. The artist's safety was her own work too.

shoal_e10_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_09.text: On Day Three Hundred Five, a sailor asked Yue whether her sixth-stage practice had made her dreams different. She said some mornings her shoulder felt the same and she dreamed about rooms she still needed to pay for. He laughed, then said that sounded disappointingly ordinary. She found the answer less disappointing than he did. Earned routes could belong to a person whose sleeping mind still worried about a badly placed cup and a missed road fare.

shoal_e10_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_10.text: The sailor invited her to watch a repaired sail tested from the public side of its licensed berth. The ordinary crew adjusted tension under its qualified foreman. A corner fluttered wrongly, and they lowered the sail to correct a stitch before the planned departure. Yue watched hands and cloth rather than searching for an energy fault. The sailor's impatience had a scheduled tide behind it. He still accepted the ordinary stop when the stitch made the problem visible.

shoal_e10_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_11.text: She remembered how easily observers applauded a successful movement and grew bored when a crew corrected it. No one cheered the lowered sail. Its actual owner paid the mender's agreed work and revised the departure. A sound crossing would depend on that unglamorous interval. Yue wrote no public lesson about it because nobody had offered their private repair record. She could learn from an ordinary scene without publishing the people in it as examples.

shoal_e10_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_12.text: At Shed Six, the steward commissioned its routine ordinary lamp-bracket check for the next scheduled date. The public exterior list showed that responsible task and its current holder. The commissioned check did not cover every later placement of packing goods. Workers would still need to keep the stated separation from flame and exit routes as stock moved. Yue knew only the offered public list. She did not climb inside the private shed to verify a world that had not invited her.

shoal_e10_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_13.text: On Day Three Hundred Six, rain brought loading under the licensed covers. Store hands moved dry packing cloth, resin-sealed bundles, and ordinary tools under their separate owner marks. The current crews kept the public approach clear while working. A passerby complained about the detour and took it. The changed weather made every dry corner valuable, just as it had made the packing-space dispute difficult. Value did not make an unsafe crowded corner larger.

shoal_e10_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_14.text: Rong's delivery plan used an existing port-owned set of freight-signal plates stored in a separate secured gallery beyond this shed lane. That set had not been part of Yue's forty-housing observations and was not a recovered Lark loan. Its owners would decide any later authorized transport. The current public cargo notice named its distinct storage. A future relay journey could need those plates without giving every visitor a reason to inspect or move them now.

shoal_e10_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_15.text: Yue had received no offer to escort that stock yet. She read the current public notice because it described a different movement through the lane, then returned to her own day. A next job could be concrete without already belonging to her. The port needed many ordinary people to staff its freight, and one certified practitioner could decline a future appointment. She liked seeing an actual resource persist somewhere she did not have to touch it.

shoal_e10_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_16.text: The lamp-bracket check at Shed Six occurred on Day Three Hundred Eight under its owner's ordinary maintenance agreement. The qualified worker recorded the checked mounting condition and the limits of the check. The steward kept the current report in the shed's lawful records. The exterior public list showed completed routine maintenance, not a guarantee against every later movement of goods. The corrected loose waste at Shed Three remained secured. Both arrangements had actual responsible people.

shoal_e10_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_17.text: The next morning arrived clear and windy. Yue left her lodging for the offered public interval near the lane, with ordinary food in her bag and her shoulder inside its existing waist limit. She expected a short witnessed movement, then a walk to the school desk. Nothing in her practice warned her of hidden future smoke. More primary pairs had not become foreknowledge. She reached the public rope before loading and greeted Yan's assigned route hand.

shoal_e10_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_18.text: Day Three Hundred Nine's current store crew had several independent tasks. One moved packing cloth; one received a resin-sealed bundle; one tended the permitted ordinary lamp inside Shed Six. The lamp's checked bracket remained mounted, but a temporary packing trolley had been moved too near its stand. That placement had occurred after the prior routine check. Yue could not see it from the public rope. A store hand inside could, and his later account would matter separately from hers.

shoal_e10_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_19.text: A cloth bundle slid when the trolley's temporary chock shifted. The store hand reached for the cloth at the wrong angle, bumped the lamp stand, and tipped its burning oil across loose material. He saw the movement and shouted the shed's ordinary fire signal. Another worker, looking from the opposite side, saw the tipped lamp and the first flame but not the chock. Their views overlapped without matching. No hidden enemy or qi flare was needed to make the ignition possible.

shoal_e10_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_20.text: Yue heard the first shout before she saw fire. Yan's route hand repeated it toward the staffed alarm post and opened the current ordinary evacuation route. The store hand inside pulled away from the spreading oil instead of trying to stamp it out through burning cloth. A qualified fire crew was called through its actual signal. Yue stepped behind the new public boundary as instructed. The body impulse to run closer arrived before she had a useful task.

shoal_e10_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_21.text: Smoke rose beneath the shed's roof edge, darker than the small exterior rag flare had been. The flame had entered resin-sealed packing stock belonging to this different owner. Shed Three's corrected waste tray remained closed and was not its source. A worker at the door held a cloth against his mouth and tried to count his coworkers. He knew them better than any visitor could. Yan asked him the actual last-seen locations while the ordinary route hand kept people moving.

shoal_e10_rejoin_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_22.text: The crew responsible for the nearby crane stopped its load at the prepared safe position and cleared its own lane. It could not leave suspended weight overhead to become a second danger while every hand ran toward fire. The qualified fire crew arrived with its current equipment and command. Other ordinary workers were assigned to the alarm route and crowd boundary. There were many people and still only a finite number of qualified actions possible at once.

shoal_e10_rejoin_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_23.text: Yue watched one fire worker test the side entrance and withdraw when heat made the planned approach unsafe. He did not become less brave by refusing it. The crew changed its entry route and called for the known remaining workers to use the farther ordinary exit if reachable. Smoke hid that side from Yue's position. She could hear commands, not certify everyone inside had obeyed. Her role as a witness ended at what the boundary and smoke actually allowed her to know.

shoal_e10_rejoin_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_24.text: The store steward wanted his inventory cabinet removed before the fire reached the partition. The fire captain told him evacuation took priority and assigned no unqualified person to enter for papers. The steward argued once, then gave the crew the actual cabinet location and stayed outside. Property could matter without outranking a current person's life. Yue did not offer a qi shield so both priorities could become effortless. The cabinet's possible loss remained possible.

shoal_e10_rejoin_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_25.text: At the public boundary, someone called Yue by name and asked her to stop the wind. She had no such qualified application. She repeated the ordinary clear-route instruction instead and helped move a small empty stool at waist height when the attendant assigned it. The wind kept blowing. A quarter-unit marker success did not give her command of weather. The stool had been a real obstruction, and removing it made one narrow route easier to use.

shoal_e10_rejoin_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_26.text: A crew woman from the medicine boat was among the onlookers, working a separately accepted stock task nearby that day. She recognized the difference between a stop signal and an invitation to crowd the equipment. Her own knowledge came through her actual prior instruction, not through a universal assumption about which communication batch everybody had received. She moved her current group's unneeded cart off the alarm lane under its owner's instruction and returned to her assigned ordinary work boundary.

shoal_e10_rejoin_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_27.text: Yan's rescue foreman role fit the ordinary route and people count, while the fire captain controlled the fire equipment. They exchanged current information without letting one shout over the other. Yue could see how roles reduced confusion when they were actually staffed. She could also see where a missing qualified hand left a task unperformed. No clerk's earlier plan could make that hand exist by naming it on a hopeful list.

shoal_e10_rejoin_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_28.text: Three workers emerged through the farther exit with a qualified guide. One had a burned sleeve and needed ordinary clinical assessment. The fourth known worker had been last seen near a rear packing shelf and remained unlocated at that moment. The count came from actual coworkers, not a tale that Yue's hearing sensed every living body. The fire captain revised the search under current heat and route conditions. The uncertainty was frightening enough without inventing invisible knowledge.

shoal_e10_rejoin_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_29.text: The clinic messenger reached the crowd with its ordinary emergency contact instructions. He did not carry a medicine that guaranteed reversal of burns. Qualified clinicians would assess those who could be safely moved to their desk or designated care point. The messenger asked for the current actual person count and reported it through the staffed route. Yue recognized him and did not interrupt his work to turn their acquaintance into a demand for comfort.

shoal_e10_rejoin_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_30.text: Inside the boundary, a worker tried to reenter for his privately owned tools. Yan stopped him and asked for their location so any later qualified salvage could consider it. The man shook with anger and fear. His tools might be his next month's earnings, not mere clutter. The route was still unsafe. Yue stayed beside him when the attendant asked, speaking only the current instruction and offering water once the messenger confirmed the ordinary public supply.

shoal_e10_rejoin_31.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_31.text: The man took the water and continued to curse. Yue did not require him to become grateful before helping him wait. She could not promise his tools would survive. The unfairness of losing a livelihood during a safety-first response remained real. A correct current boundary could protect a person and let important property burn. The fire's pressure made people want a hero who could abolish that trade. Yue had only a body with a narrow tested range.

shoal_e10_rejoin_32.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_32.text: The fire captain sent a qualified team toward the rear approach after confirming the ordinary cribbed support and a usable exit. Yan kept the public observers farther back because a roof section could fall into the earlier waiting place. Everyone moved, including Yue. The new position hid more of the interior. She would not later describe the search as if she had watched every step. Losing a viewing angle was part of staying outside a danger she could not qualify away.

shoal_e10_rejoin_33.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_33.text: From there, she saw flame reach the upper resin stack and heard the structure's dry cracking. The team withdrew with the fourth worker, alive and unable to bear weight on one leg. Qualified care took him immediately through the prepared route. His injury would need actual assessment and funded care; rescue had not made him whole. Yue felt relief so sharply that she nearly forgot the three people already waiting for theirs. The count was complete, and the losses were still unfolding.

shoal_e10_rejoin_34.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_34.text: The rescued worker's partner arrived from a different current job. She asked for him and chose to accompany him under the clinician's instructions. Nobody required her to make a public statement before reaching his side. The fire captain confirmed that no known worker remained inside, while keeping the possibility of unrecorded visitors subject to actual information. A known count could be complete without magical omniscience. The store steward checked his current visitor record and named none.

shoal_e10_rejoin_35.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_35.text: With the known evacuation completed, the qualified command shifted to limiting spread and protecting defined reachable material. It still could not preserve every owner record, tool, resin bundle, and neighboring workroom. Two ordinary support roles had been requested under the current plan: guide a consenting receiving group through the safe long route, or join a short waist-height water relay behind the inspected protection line. Both would need current assignment and an early stop if conditions changed.

shoal_e10_rejoin_36.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_36.text: Yue could accept one role within her bodily clearance or remain an ordinary waiting observer. Neither required a talisman, overhead catch, or movement into smoke. The guide role might get owners and their lawful access information to a reachable record store in time. The water relay might keep a narrow partition cooler while a qualified crew protected a different stock bay. The fire captain described each concrete task without pretending either would save the whole shed.

shoal_e10_rejoin_37.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_37.text: Before any assignment, Yan asked Yue to repeat her current limit. Supported waist work remained permitted; overhead load did not. The recent grip check had matched her narrow baseline, and any renewed sensation ended her task. The fire captain cared because an injured helper would consume qualified attention needed elsewhere. Yue answered without announcing her stage to the crowd. Six primary pairs did not make her exempt from the same ordinary route and stop instructions.

shoal_e10_rejoin_38.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_38.text: The two support groups had their own willing people and owners. The consenting guide group could walk only the inspected long route, with records opened by lawful custodians at the destination. The water relay had assigned ordinary pails and a strict waist-height passing limit. No one asked Yue to purchase a crew from her wage purse. Qualified rescue and clinical care remained separately staffed and funded under their current accounts. Her offered work would be voluntary, bounded emergency assistance.

shoal_e10_rejoin_39.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_39.text: The steward looked at the two reachable places and asked again whether more people could simply do both. The fire captain said the current route and equipment capacity, not goodwill alone, limited the assignments. Additional untrained people would narrow exits or block the relay. A nearby ordinary helper declined after checking his own hand injury. Another accepted a defined cart-clearing task. Refusals and smaller jobs helped the command know what its actual people could do.

shoal_e10_rejoin_40.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_40.text: Yue remembered the crate on the tide and the audience hour in Song Mei's room. Those choices had prepared her to name a limit; they had not prepared her to feel one beneath smoke. The guide group waited on one side, the relay supervisor on the other. She could describe a small measured useful output precisely and still find a burning shed too large to grasp. She asked where each role would stop before deciding where she would begin.

shoal_e10_rejoin_41.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_rejoin_41.text: The first independently observed lamp spill remained in the workers' current accounts, separate from the corrected earlier exterior flare. The fire would later need an ignition record and a careful distinction between cause and responsibility. Right now, a qualified command needed a willing person for one of two safe support tasks. Yue turned from the unreachable flame toward those actual people, ready to choose work small enough for her to perform and large enough to change what they could still preserve.

shoal_e10_child_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_child_01.text: A little boy stood beside the boundary holding one shoe. He had lost the other while leaving a room, and his parent was searching the safe area for him. The attendant reunited them without sending anyone back toward flame for the shoe. Yue watched the parent check his face before asking about it.

shoal_e10_child_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e10_child_02.text: The boy wanted to return because the shoes had been new. His parent said they would stay together now and argue about shoes later. Their disagreement continued while the fire crew worked. Yue found it grounding. People were particular beneath disaster, wanting the things that made their own day recognizable.
